claim.quote: First evidence for neutrinoless double beta decay is observed giving first evidence for lepton number violation.

date.locator: arXiv stamp on the first page
date.note: arXiv v1 date; the journal version is Mod. Phys. Lett. A 16 (2001) 2409 (DOI 10.1142/S0217732301005825).

key_value_text.quote: The half-life of the process is found with the Bayesian method to be T_{1/2}^{0ν} = (0.8 - 18.3) x 10^{25} y (95% c.l.) with a best value of 1.5 x 10^{25} y.

name: Evidence for Neutrinoless Double Beta Decay
notes: Authors: Klapdor-Kleingrothaus, Dietz, Harney, Krivosheina (the paper's affiliations are the Max-Planck-Institut fuer Kernphysik and the Radiophysical-Research Institute, Nishnii-Novgorod). It is a claim by part of the collaboration, not the collaboration's headline result.

The CUORICINO PRL (hep-ex/0501034) calls it 'the claimed discovery of the decay of 76Ge reported by a subset of the Heidelberg-Moscow collaboration' and states: 'This claim has been contested by various authors [14, 29, 30] and also by other members of the same Heidelberg-Moscow Collaboration [31].'

GERDA's Phase I paper (arXiv:1307.4720) states: "Part of HdM published a claim to have observed". The same group's 2004 paper (hep-ph/0404088, full data 1990-2003) reports the confidence level improved to 4.2 sigma in its abstract; it is not recorded as a separate result.

significance.quote: The evidence for this decay mode is 97% (2.2σ) with the Bayesian method, and 99.8% c.l. (3.1σ) with the method recommended by the Particle Data Group.
significance.value: 97% (2.2 sigma) with the Bayesian method; 99.8% c.l. (3.1 sigma) with the method recommended by the Particle Data Group

summary.plain: Four members of the Heidelberg-Moscow team re-analysed the 1990-2000 data and reported evidence for neutrinoless double beta decay in germanium-76, at 2.2 to 3.1 sigma depending on the method. The claim was published by part of the collaboration only and was later tested by other germanium experiments.
summary.technical: Bayesian re-analysis of 54.98 kg y (Aug 1990 - May 2000): 97 % (2.2 sigma) with the Bayesian method, 99.8 % c.l. (3.1 sigma) with the PDG-recommended method; T1/2 = (0.8-18.3)e25 yr (95 % c.l.), best value 1.5e25 yr; <m> = 0.11-0.56 eV (95 % c.l.). Not the collaboration's own headline result: see the notes.

title: Evidence for Neutrinoless Double Beta Decay
why_it_matters: The only claimed signal of neutrinoless double beta decay in germanium; it motivated GERDA, whose first phase was designed to test it.
